## What is LepiSense?

LepiSense is a lightweight, smaller version of the [AMI system](ami.qmd), designed to make automated imaging of moths and butterflies more accessible, scalable and easier to deploy. Where AMI is built for high-volume, long-term global monitoring, LepiSense focuses on **lower-cost, portable deployments** for more experimental or resource-limited settings.

It builds on everything learned from AMI, while putting simplicity, quick testing and smaller-scale data collection first.

## Why LepiSense matters

Traditional moth and butterfly surveys are often labour-intensive, depend on specialist expertise, and vary between sites and observers. LepiSense collects **standardised, automated photos** without needing the full AMI set-up. It's especially useful for:

- pilot and feasibility studies;
- student or short-term research projects;
- monitoring on a small budget;
- adding local sampling alongside larger AMI deployments;
- testing models, workflows and new AI classifiers before scaling up.

## Where it's being used

LepiSense is in an **early testing phase**, with pilot deployments planned or under way across UKCEH projects: small test plots, feasibility deployments, testing alongside AMI traps, and calibration in climate-controlled chambers. Wider field deployments will follow.

## How it works

LepiSense follows the same principles as AMI:

- **Lightweight hardware:** a compact imaging unit, low-power LEDs to attract insects, a small housing and a basic onboard computer for scheduling and logging, designed to be carried and set up quickly.
- **Collecting data:** photos of moths and other night-flying insects on flexible schedules; well suited to short deployments; needs less storage than AMI.
- **Analysis:** works with the same image models as AMI, through our [open-source toolkit](https://github.com/NERC-CEH/ceh-biomonitoring).

The aim is a system that is **affordable, robust, easy to transport, compatible with AMI data**, and suitable for wide use in future student, partner and citizen-science programmes.
